proposal.claim: Removing reconnect_t1_3d from the mechanics-only best leaves the sphere intact (protr_peak stays within 1.00-1.05, analyst_consensus still 'sphere').
proposal.predicted: sphere, protr_peak ~1.0, score within noise of e8e350
proposal.why: T1 topology swaps are solo-insufficient; if the sphere is really surface-minimization by shape_energy_3d, reconnection is inert and its removal gives a strictly simpler sufficient mechanism — a stronger result than the 3-op stack.

proposal.claim: Adding divide_3d (the growth cluster's operator) on top of the mechanics-only best breaks spherical symmetry: protr_peak rises above 1.2 and a new non-sphere phenotype (bud/protrusion) enters the map.
proposal.predicted: budding/protrusion phenotype, protr_peak >1.2, first non-sphere point (coverage >0%)
proposal.why: divide_3d was solo-insufficient, but proliferation supplies the volume that surface tension alone cannot; coupling growth to shape_energy_3d is the classic route from sphere to protrusion and combines a mechanism that failed alone in a different cluster.

proposal.claim: Seeding seed_mesh_3d with an anisotropic (polarized/elongated) initial mesh instead of an isotropic ball yields an oriented ellipsoid/protrusion aligned to the seed axis, protr_peak >1.1, rather than relaxing back to a sphere.
proposal.why: The reference morphology is not isotropic; grounding the initial condition in the reference's polarized geometry tests whether shape_energy_3d preserves an imposed axis or erases it, moving the composition closer to what the reference model actually does.
